name: Damper (Australian Campfire Bread)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: scant ¼ cup water (more and it will be as tough as an old boot)

steps: Add water, then mix and form into a round loaf.
Dig a 1 foot-deep hole near a fire, and fill it with 2 shovels of hot coals and ash.
Add damper mixture to a greased camp oven (traditional cast iron round pot with lid).
Cook in the hole for a maximum of 40 minutes. If undercooked it will be flat and rubbery.
Your first try may be inedible. Keep trying, you'll soon be an expert.

culture.text: Damper is Australian bushman's bread, made while camping or "waltzing matilda" (carrying a swag around looking for work). It is meant to be made outside by a campfire.
